clue.text: Quieten drug smuggler, going around very loudly

indicators.note: the smuggler's word goes around the musical marking, enclosing it

parts.note: a mule is slang for someone who carries drugs across borders
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: An order to silence a drug smuggler as they circle round making a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very loudly' is the musical marking fortissimo, written FF on a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To muffle a sound is to deaden it, making it quieter.

clue.text: Characters in farm I'd offer place in the field

indicators.note: the letters of the answer are characters found within the phrase

explanation.surface: Something a farmer might be offered to plant in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-OFF is a cricket fielding position, near the bowler on the off side. 'field' suggests farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-off is a named position in the cricket field where a fielder stands.

clue.text: Cookware from Spooner's inquisitive admirer

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped initial sounds, so the two words trade first letters

parts.note: prying means nosily inquisitive
a fan is an admirer

explanation.surface: A cooking pan supplied by a nosy fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening P and F of PRYING FAN to get FRYING PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying pan is a shallow pan, a standard item of kitchen cookware.

clue.text: Cub leader is dishonest about working with leader of Scouts

indicators.note: the dishonest word wraps about the working word

parts.note: someone who lies is being dishonest
on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of Scouts

explanation.surface: A Cub Scout leader is accused of lying while working with the head of Scouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cub leader' points to the Scout movement; the cub is a lion's. LIES goes about ON (LI-ON-ES), then S.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is the female lion that leads and rears its cubs.

clue.text: Star after time with friends abroad makes waves

indicators.note: the star comes after the time letter, so the abbreviation is placed first

parts.note: the Sun is our nearest star
amis is French for friends

explanation.surface: A celebrity, having spent time with foreign pals, causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' and 'makes waves' read as celebrity gossip; the star is the Sun and 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are huge sea waves set off by undersea earthquakes.

clue.text: Made an error on record — this brings back discomfort

parts.note: to slip up is to make an error
a disc is a gramophone record

explanation.surface: Someone flubbed a recording and is now regretting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings back' sounds like recalling; it is pain in the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipped disc is a spinal injury that causes back pain.

clue.text: Smarter bit of couture: it tantalises when twirling

indicators.note: twirling turns the hidden stretch round, so it reads backwards
only a stretch of the words is used, a bit taken from them

explanation.surface: A fashion item turns heads when a model twirls on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' finds REITTAN across coutuRE IT TANtalises; 'when twirling' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and neat in appearance, so nattier is smarter.

clue.text: US university, without hesitation, showing excellence

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the university goes round the hesitation

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An American college shows excellence by never faltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; here it has its old sense of outside, so it signals enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence deserving praise.

clue.text: Split peas cooked with speed

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of peas are reworked

parts.note: rate means speed, as in rate of travel

explanation.surface: Split peas prepared in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split peas' reads as one food, but 'Split' is the definition and only 'peas' is anagrammed by 'cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: To split up is to separate, and separate as an adjective means split apart.

clue.text: Starter of dates or try bananas — this can make fruit crumble

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word dates is taken as the start
going bananas means going crazy, so the letters of or try are scrambled

explanation.surface: A recipe: begin with dates, or try bananas, and you get a fruit crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges OR TRY into RYROT, after D. 'fruit crumble' looks like a pudding; here 'fruit' is the fungus's fruiting body and crumble is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay of timber; its fruiting bodies spread it and leave the wood crumbling.

clue.text: Talent with hip-hop cover to give away

parts.note: a gift is a natural talent
rap is the vocal style of hip-hop music

explanation.surface: A musician's flair for hip-hop lets them make a cover version to give away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gift wrap is decorative paper for covering a present before handing it over.

clue.text: Tot getting hint in part of index, perhaps

parts.note: a tot of spirit is a small measure, as is a finger of whisky
a tip is a useful hint

explanation.surface: A small child is given a clue in a section of a book's index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' suggests a child and 'index' a book; here a tot is a drink measure and the index is the forefinger.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger has a tip, so the fingertip is one part of it.

clue.text: Alluring people work briefly north of Barnet?

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above, north of, the second

parts.note: to temp is to do temporary work
Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and tresses are hair

explanation.surface: Seductive types temp for a while just north of Barnet, a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barnet' is a north London district, but in rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Temptresses are women who allure or seduce.

clue.text: Bury FC

definitions.meaning: ... Milan is an Italian football club

explanation.surface: Bury FC is a real English football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the name of Bury Football Club, but each word is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter means to put into a grave, and Internazionale (Inter) is a famous football club.

clue.text: Maybe Andy Warhol stormed in unsteadily after job

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the job word, which therefore goes first

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: moving unsteadily suggests the letters of stormed in wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Andy Warhol lurches in after landing a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' rearranges the letters of 'stormed in'; 'after' places them behind the job word.
explanation.definitionFit: Warhol, the pop artist, is often classed as a postmodern artist; 'Maybe' marks him as one example.

clue.text: Strange realities figure in the Bible

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of realities form something odd and new

explanation.surface: Odd truths appear in Scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites, descendants of Jacob, are a people throughout the Old Testament.

clue.text: Use thread to mend frame

definitions.meaning: to ... a tear is to sew it closed
to stitch someone up is to frame them for a crime

explanation.surface: Sewing to repair a picture frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitch up means both to sew together and, as slang, to falsely incriminate.

clue.text: It's hard to say to utter swine, out drinking gallons

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the gallons letter, as if swallowing it
out here means wrong or disordered, so to utter swine is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something shouted at a drunken pig that is guzzling gallons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TO UTTER SWINE and 'drinking' slips G into it. 'It's hard to say' reads as a shrug; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue-twister is a phrase built to be difficult to pronounce.

clue.text: You reportedly lead attack, getting reprimand

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word You is said and its sound written as a letter

parts.note: the word you is said aloud and sounds like the letter U
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: You lead an assault and get told off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a verb; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to scold or reprimand them.

clue.text: Delay punishment given to criminal

parts.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence
an old lag is a habitual convict

explanation.surface: A criminal's sentence is postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is an interval or delay between two events.

clue.text: Gather case of Sancerre will rise in value

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to meet is to gather together

indicators.note: the case is the outside, so the first and last letters of Sancerre

explanation.surface: A wine collector expects a case of Sancerre to go up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to hold it in high regard, to value it.

clue.text: Ruffian wanting good doctor? One's on hand

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the good letter is missing from the ruffian

parts.note: a thug is a violent ruffian
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A thug wants a decent doctor, perhaps after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's on hand' sounds like 'available'; it means a digit on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb is one of the digits of the hand.

clue.text: Open a place to drink in Paris?

parts.note: un is French for a, as 'in Paris' signals
a bar is somewhere to have a drink

explanation.surface: Opening a bar in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' marks the French reading: 'un bar' is French for 'a bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbar a door is to remove its bar and so open it.

clue.text: Charlie cuts additives put in food hampers

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the additives word, sitting inside it

parts.note: E-numbers are coded additives listed on food labels
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie removes additives that have been put into packed food hampers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampers' looks like picnic baskets; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To encumber is to weigh down or impede, so encumbers and hampers are synonyms.

clue.text: Jewish scholar's underwear taken in robbery

indicators.note: the underwear is placed within the robbery word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A scholar's underwear was among the loot in a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebraist is an expert in the Hebrew language and its texts.

clue.text: Nepali high in the mountains

indicators.note: high here means intoxicated, so the letters of Nepali are jumbled

explanation.surface: A person from Nepal up in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' seems to belong with the mountains; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine describes things found in or relating to high mountains.

clue.text: Adam's garden is planted in March

indicators.note: is is set into the march word like a seedling

parts.note: a parade is a march

explanation.surface: Adam's garden is sown in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden, where Adam lived, is also called Paradise.

clue.text: Shiny silver coat of ladylike American

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: a coat is the outer layer, so the outside letters of ladylike are used

explanation.surface: An American lady wears a shiny silver coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam means gleaming, giving off light, which is what shiny things do.
